text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore Parliament backs report which found four opposition members from the Singapore Democratic Party guilty of contempt of Parliament.
- Singapore formally submits to World Trade Orgnaisation (WTO) improved offer to liberalise basic telecommunications market by year 2000.
- Chairman of WTO first ministerial conference Yeo Cheow Tong called on members to reach agreement on unresolved issues.
- Shipping tycoon Tung Chee Hwa wins Hong Kong's chief executive job in landslide victory.
- Malaysian conglomerate Sime Darby Bhd gets approval from Malaysia's central bank to start negotiations to acquire majority stake in Oriental Bank Bhd.
- U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin says U.S. should not use dollar to cut trade deficit.
- Futures contracts fall on Standard & Poor 500 pulls down Asian markets on Wednesday.
- Hong Kong's business and political community welcomes shipping magnate Tung Chee Hwa's big win to become first chief executive.
- Plunge in S&P 500 futures rattles markets in Asia.
- Wearnes International teams up with Jakarta's Star Surya group to distribute Rolls Royce, Bentley, Daimler nad Jaguar cars in Indonesia.
- Property company Wing Tai to reduce its interest in a previously announced S$200 million deal to buy Cairnhill Hotel from 75 percent to half.
